whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Perfect
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in standard injury cases. That means your recovery isn't limited to just medical bills and lost wages.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. You can get legal help without worrying about hourly rates or retainers.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Laguna Niguel?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government agency or public entity was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not blocked entirely.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in Laguna Niguel?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Crown Valley Parkway, Golden Lantern, Alicia Parkway, and Moulton Parkway, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?
items.answer: No. Our free case review costs nothing, and if you choose to move forward, we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. That's different from some other states, and it's one reason it helps to speak with an attorney familiar with California law.
